en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Darkness at Night 11.
The Training Rule on Darkness at Night:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a relative of the nun Bhaddā Kāpilānī’s pupil had come from a village to Sāvatthī on some business.
Then that nun stood and conversed with that man alone with one person in the darkness of night, where there was no lamp.
Those nuns who were of few desires... [as above] ...were indignant, complained, and became vexed, saying:
“How indeed can a bhikkhunī, in the dark of night and without a lamp, stand together with a man and converse, one-on-one? … [The Buddha asked:
“Is it true, monks, that a bhikkhunī stands together with a man and converses, one-on-one, in the dark of night and without a lamp?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How, monks, can a bhikkhunī, in the darkness of night and without a lamp, stand or converse alone with a man?
This, monks, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence…” [and so on].
And furthermore, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule as follows:
“Whichever nun, in the darkness of night and without a lamp, should stand or converse alone with a man, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whichever nun” means:
Whichever [nun] of whatever kind... [as before] ...a bhikkhunī...
[as before] ...this is the bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"In the darkness of night" means when the sun has set.
"Without a lamp" means...
In the absence of light.
A "man" means a human being, not a *yakkha*, not a *peta*, and not an animal; one who is conscious and capable of standing and conversing.
"Saddhim" means together. "Ekena ekaṃ" means one with one.
It is both a man and a nun.
"Should stand together" means:
if she stands within arm's reach of the man, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should converse" means:
if she converses while standing within arm's reach of a man, there is an offense of *pācittiya*.
If she stands or converses after having left arm's reach, there is an offense of *dukkaṭa*.
If one stands together with or converses with a yakkha, a peta, a paṇḍaka, or one who has the appearance of a human being but is actually an animal, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if one has any other person who understands as a companion.
If she is indifferent,
or if she is distracted by something else while standing or conversing,
or if she is insane;
"For one who is a first offender":
thus ends the first training rule.
